title: Probability-One Differentials Beyond Two-Round SPNs
summary: Theory and non-existence criteria for probability-one differentials cover two-round SPNs; extending them to more rounds, especially four rounds, remains open.

formal_statement.body: For substitution-permutation networks (SPNs), the existing theory and non-existence criteria for probability-one differentials are developed for two rounds. The unresolved task is to generalize this theory and these criteria to SPNs with more than two rounds while preserving the exact probability-one differential setting. In particular, for four-round SPNs, the proposed direction replaces individual S-boxes with two-round superboxes and requires establishing that a superbox does not have maximal boomerang uniformity.

scope.domain: Differential and structural cryptanalysis of substitution-permutation networks and two-round superboxes.
parameters: SPN round count: two rounds are covered, while more than two rounds, particularly four, are targeted
Differential probability: restricted to exactly one
Superbox depth: two SPN rounds in the proposed four-round approach
scope.unresolved_remainder: Extend the probability-one differential theory and non-existence criteria to SPNs with more than two rounds; for four rounds, establish that a two-round superbox does not have maximal boomerang uniformity.

citations.label: On Perfect Linear Approximations and Differentials over Two-Round SPNs

progress.summary: The source presents two-round SPNs as the current boundary and identifies extension of the probability-one differential case to more rounds as worthwhile future work. For four rounds, it proposes two-round superboxes and highlights non-maximal boomerang uniformity as a technical requirement.
citation_labels: Christof Beierle et al., On Perfect Linear Approximations and Differentials over Two-Round SPNs
